This happened last Saturday. Sorry for the book, there is a less therapeutic TL;DR at the bottom.

I was out with the family doing some shopping and was given the opportunity to skip back-to-school shopping at Target and go with my son to SportsMANs Warehouse (sort of like Cabelas). We are out in the 2 month old family car, a 2015 Subaru Outback. Now driving into the parking lot I am looking for convenient, but safe, parking as I don’t want to be responsible for any door dings on my wife’s new car. Here is the FU, I spot a disabled parking spot and think. That is kinda like an end spot and park next to it. I normally drive a pickup and am not used to the smaller Outback and end up not executing the best parking job in the world. I jump out and see it is not good, but acceptable and decide to go into the store thinking in my head, “Meh, nothing will happen.” After a delightful 30 minutes browsing sporting good my young son and I leave, him clutching our new green glow-stick. He gets in the opposite side of the car and I go around to buckle him up. At this moment my phone starts ringing as my wife is calling to tell me she is ready to be picked up at Target. As I open the door to buckle my son, my brain stops working. What the fuck is that on the door? Is it a door ding…nope that is the biggest fucking door ding ever, as in door dent. It looks like someone began to open their door and then kicked it at full force right into my new car. After briefly thinking about not telling my wife I answer and tell her there is a massive dent in her car. She says you’re joking right? Oh I wish I was…nope. I don’t know what to say.

The car parked next to me is a van with sliding doors and clearly not the offending vehicle. Looking around in desperation I notice cameras on the roof of the store. I head inside to ask for surveillance video and call the police. The police politely tell me that they don’t respond to calls regarding door dings in parking lots and I should take it up with my insurance. But I plead and explain this is not an ordinary door ding, but the biggest motherfucking door ding in the history of mankind. That someone had mercilessly beaten my poor defenseless vehicle with their door. I also mentioned I was asking for video and he reluctantly agreed to send out an officer, but said it was windy and that unless it was malicious there was little they could do.

The lovely loss prevention employee of the store efficiently pulled up the video and relayed to me that there was a black car that pulled up next to my car, the back door appeared to hit the car and everyone got out to look at my vehicle. After which they all got back into their car (family of four) and drove away. I felt so violated and knew my darling wife was going to be pissed once she saw I had not safely parked in an end spot, as she had religiously done for the past two months. During this time my wife and daughter arrived from Target on foot and patiently waited in the car for the police to arrive.

After the officer’s arrival he spent a long time in the store only to emerge with two printouts and a DVD. It appeared the suspects with super human door opening ability had not actually left after hitting my car, but had just moved to another spot to ensure I could not figure out who had caused the damage. They then proceeded to walk into the store as a family, and have a great photo taken on the HD security camera. Unfortunately they did not buy anything from the store, so no luck on a name, and the picture of their car leaving was not good enough to get a plate number. The officer graciously let me take pictures of the printout and informed me he would try to find them, but since all he had was a photo, I should not get my hopes up.

I had a very depressing ride home knowing my lazy moment put the car in a position where it was damaged when an extra 20 seconds of walking would have drastically reduced the chance of this happening. To add insult to injury I notice that the security photo of them leaving had my wife in it. Meaning, these fuckers actually walked out of the store, and right by us as we were standing in shock by our vehicle. After a somewhat sad afternoon and filing a hit and run claim with our insurance (the second one in the past six months), my wife asked me for the picture. BTW, she deserves a medal for kindly telling me it was not my fault, which is true, but I still felt terrible. Apparently there is a website called The Facebook or something like that and she wanted to post the mugs of the Mom and Dad who did us wrong. Sure darling if it will make you happy... Ten minutes later a “private message” came in asking why were we looking the folks in the photo. This online friend apparently may know the real world perpetrators. Well after brief exchanges it was confirmed! Off we went on a very rare dinner date knowing life was a little bit better. A friend who I had been venting to (he used to be an insurance adjuster) was so excited when I shared the news. Since I was on a date I asked for a favor and he came through with an address for the dodgy couple with the aid of his professional cyber stalking wife. I passed said information onto our friendly police officer.

11 am the next morning the doorbell rings. The fine officer did stop by the address we found and said he made contact with “they-who-must-not-be-named” and whom spun a nice story (probably true) about the wind catching the doors causing the impact, and they did not know what to do (probably not so true). Officer Awesome told them their obligations and let them off with a lecture (honestly I would probably have done the same) in exchange for admitting fault and providing insurance information. So we are getting the car repaired and a large part is being repainted, but we don’t have to pay a hit and run deductible, and we cracked the case! Not really a happy ending, but less sucky.

TL;DR: Failed to park my wife’s new car in an end spot as she always does, and came back to a fist sized dent in the door and no note. Thanks to security footage and Facebook a friend recognized the couple and did the right thing in giving us the name. The police tracked them down and got the appropriate information. Insurance is taking care of it, but the car still has a boo boo…for now.
